summary.text: Ann-Marie Hermans has been a Liberal member of the Legislative Council for South-Eastern Metropolitan Region since the 2022 election, having stood for Family First in the same region in 2006. A former head of an academic department at Presbyterian Ladies' College, she has held shadow roles in emergency services, WorkCover and the TAC, and education, and is now Shadow Assistant Minister for Community Safety. She is recontesting South-Eastern Metropolitan in 2026, second on the Liberal ticket according to Wikipedia.

summary.text: Brandon Hoult leads the Sustainable Australia Party ticket for South-Eastern Metropolitan Region in the Legislative Council at the 2026 Victorian election. The party says he grew up in Melbourne's south-east and still lives there, and is campaigning mainly on housing affordability, public services and local planning. A Brandon Hoult has stood for the party, or as an independent, at several state, federal and Bayside council elections since 2010, including at the top of its 2022 ticket for this region.

summary.text: David Limbrick represents South-Eastern Metropolitan Region in the Legislative Council for the Libertarian Party, known as the Liberal Democrats when he was first elected in 2018. He left the Council in April 2022 to run for the Senate, and after that bid failed a joint sitting of Parliament returned him to his old seat in June 2022. He was re-elected at the November 2022 state election and is standing again in South-Eastern Metropolitan in 2026.

prior_roles.note: Reappointed by a joint sitting in June 2022 to fill the vacancy left by his own resignation, then re-elected in November 2022.

summary.text: Lee Tarlamis is a Labor member of the Legislative Council for South-Eastern Metropolitan Region, which he first represented from 2010 until he lost his place at the 2014 election. After working as an adviser in the Andrews government he came back in 2020 to fill the vacancy Gavin Jennings left, and he is now Government Whip in the upper house. He holds the Medal of the Order of Australia (OAM) and heads Labor's group (D) for the region on the 2026 ballot paper.

summary.text: Matthew Kirwan is the Greens' lead candidate for South-Eastern Metropolitan Region in the 2026 Legislative Council election. A public policy professional who says he has always lived in Melbourne's south-east, he was elected to the City of Greater Dandenong council in 2012 as its first Greens councillor. He has stood for the Greens at several state and federal elections, including Dandenong in 2010 and 2022 and Isaacs in 2025.
